title: Format-agnostic Weight Adapter + Deterministic Provenance Canary
creator: Anika Patel
description: Build a format-agnostic weights adapter and a deterministic provenance canary to streamline onboarding of open-source LLM checkpoints. The adapter must accept heterogeneous inputs (Hugging Face sharded checkpoints, safetensors, merged zips, delta patches, and model zoo manifests), verify signatures, assemble sharded shards reliably, and produce a reproducible canonical artifact (runtime-ready .rwt or equivalent). The canary will deterministically convert a representative subset of variants (fp16, int8-quantized, 4-bit) inside a hermetic sandbox and produce byte-level fingerprints and performance profiles to auto-publish into the model catalog. This ticket focuses on the end-to-end flow from intake artifact -> conversion sandbox -> deterministic fingerprinting -> smoke-execution on micro-canary runners -> profile publish + rollback gates.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Adapter can ingest at least three source formats: HF sharded .bin+config, safetensors, and delta patch bundles and produce identical canonical artifacts given identical source content.
2) Conversion sandbox (WASM/container) produces deterministic build: same input -> same artifact hash across runs.
3) Automated micro-canary executes converted model on two runtime variants (baseline fp16 and quantized int8) and records latency/p99, token/sec, and end-to-end correctness against evaluation prompt set.
4) Conversion artifacts include a signed provenance manifest (content-addressable hashes for source files, conversion recipe, toolchain version). Manifest is uploaded to the model catalog and visible in the profile UI.
5) Failure modes produce actionable error codes and map to rollout gates (block pin publish, mark as manual review).
implementation_notes:
- Use a thin adapter abstraction with plugin-based format handlers (hf_checkpoint_handler, safetensors_handler, delta_apply).
- Perform assembly using content-addressable temporary store and deterministic ordering of shards.
- Conversion runs inside a hermetic WASM sandbox packaged as a container image to ensure reproducible environment (pinned toolchain versions).
- All rng or non-determinism must be controlled: set seeds, disable nondet threads, and normalize metadata timestamps.
- Compute canonical artifact hash using SHA-256 over a canonicalized byte layout (header fields normalized).
- Sign manifest with onboarding service key; integrate with KMS for production signing and optional HSM for enterprise Private installs.
- Persist conversion telemetry and profiling to the onboarding telemetry table for audit and later regression detection.
rollout_plan:
Phase A (internal): run on nightly inbound weights for 7 days against sample of community models. Manual review of edge cases.
Phase B (canary): enable auto-convert-and-profile for low-risk models (non-LLM family or <10GB) and auto-publish draft profiles to catalog in draft state.
Phase C (safe-autopublish): tighten rules and enable pinned publish for models that pass deterministic canary and safety checks.
Safety gates: signature verification, deterministic reproducibility, smoke test CPU/GPU correctness. Manual override available in Console for blocked pins.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: nondeterministic conversions due to floating-point math or environment differences. Mitigation: pin toolchain, run conversions in same runtime container, and include a deterministic normalization step.
- Risk: malformed sharded checkpoints that lead to silent corruption. Mitigation: strict checksums per shard, reassembly verification, and clear error mapping.
- Risk: long-running conversion for very large models. Mitigation: chunked conversion with streaming checksums and timeouts; surface progress to Console.
- Risk: leakage of source PII or licensing issues. Mitigation: manifest includes license metadata and a policy check step; redact PII in telemetry; require legal review if license ambiguous.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for each format handler with fuzzed shards.
- Determinism test: run conversion 5x across different worker hosts and assert identical artifact hash.
- Micro-canary E2E: run converted artifact against the runtime smoke suite (small prompt set) on both fp16 and int8 variants.
- Integration: publish manifest to staging catalog and assert that Console displays provenance and that rollouts respect gate state.
- Load test: convert 50 models in parallel in staging to identify resource bottlenecks.

2025-02-27 - QA (Sofia Li): Determinism tests passing on small artifacts, failing on deep-sharded checkpoints > 32 files due to implicit threading in converter. Marked follow-up (ENG-203405) to harden converter threading model.

Next steps: finalize KMS signing integration, add delta-apply plugin for patch bundles, and enable Phase A nightly.
